characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss Sigma Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FE-SEM) operated at 20 kV, fitted with high-speed X-ray energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS)
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the Ni-containing sample annealed at 500 °C the SEM micrographs show dark elongated B2 stringer bands in a lighter γ + κ matrix and coarse grain-boundary B2 particles (GB-B2).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Specimens polished and etched in a 5% nital solution
characterization_methods.purpose: microstructure observation (phase morphology and distribution) and EDS composition analysis
characterization_methods.technique: Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FE-SEM) with X-ray energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS)

characterization_methods.key_findings: TEM bright-field images show nano-disk B2 particles in the α matrix and cuboid κ particles in the γ matrix; for the Ni-containing sample at 500 °C the γ matrix contains nano-sized cuboidal κ.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Thin foils prepared by twin-jet electro-polishing in a mixture of 10% perchloric acid and 90% ethanol with an applied potential of 25 V
characterization_methods.purpose: characterization of the ordered phases (κ-carbide and B2) and their morphology
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) - selected-area diffraction patterns (SADPs) and bright-field (BF) imaging

characterization_methods.key_findings: For the Ni-containing alloy annealed at 500 °C, composite hardness values were γ + κ = 6.7 GPa, B2 stringer = 10.1 GPa, γ + κ + B2 = 8.8 GPa; the technique measures a compound (matrix + particles) hardness rather than isolated nano-precipitates.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Constant loading/unloading rate of 500 μN s-1 up to a maximum load of 10000 μN, hold time 20 s; each phase measured at least 25 times, in arrays of 50-70 indentations
characterization_methods.purpose: measurement of the nanohardness of individual phases and phase combinations

analytical_models.equation_role: fitting simulated unit-cell volumes to obtain the bulk modulus
analytical_models.model_note: Various unit cell volumes were simulated and fitted using a Murnaghan equation of state to calculate the bulk modulus.

analytical_models.equation_role: determination of C11, C12 and C44 from longitudinal/transverse sound velocities
analytical_models.model_name: Elastic constants from acoustic phonon slopes (first method)
analytical_models.model_note: The [100] direction gives C11 and C44; the [111] direction gives C12 (equations 1-3).

analytical_models.equation_role: determination of elastic constants from energy changes under volume-conserving orthorhombic and monoclinic distortions
analytical_models.model_note: A volume-conserving orthorhombic distortion gives C11-C12; a monoclinic distortion gives C44; ref. 40 scheme used for the additional tetragonal constants C13, C33, C66 (equations 4-7).

analytical_models.equation_role: calculation of bulk modulus B0, anisotropy factor Ca, shear modulus G and Young's moduli E100 and E111 from the elastic constants
analytical_models.model_note: Equations 8-12 used to derive B0, Ca, G, E100 and E111.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: For structure optimization, Brillouin zone integrations on an 18x18x18 Monkhorst-Pack grid; real-space grid with 50 Ryd energy cut-off for charge density; augmentation charges expanded up to 600 Ryd; a 30x30x30 grid with 60 Ryd energy cut-off used for the electronic density of states and formation-energy calculations; dynamical matrices from linear response in the harmonic approximation; density of states by the tetrahedron method with a 30x30x30 mesh.
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Ultrasoft pseudopotentials created based on a modified Rappe-Rabe-Kaxiras-Joannopoulos (RRKJ) scheme
computational_details.simulation_method: Ab-initio Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations (Hohenberg-Kohn method), generalized gradient approximation (GGA) of Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) in spin-polarized manner
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated lattice parameter of ordered FeAl-B2 (spin-polarized and non-spin) was slightly less than the experimental value but in good agreement; the calculated lattice constant for Fe3AlC was larger than that for Fe3Al-L1'2, agreeing with reported experimental observations.

interfaces.interface_notes: B2 phase formed in the γ-phase is described as having flat interfaces and sharp edges with an average size of ≈1.4 μm (b0026); no coherence/OR data specific to the 500 °C condition are reported.
interfaces.phase_evolution: On annealing the solution-treated Ni-containing alloy at 500 °C, the prior α (ferrite) phase was replaced by B2 stringer bands, nano-sized cuboidal κ-carbide (L1'2) formed in the γ matrix, and coarse B2 particles (2–7 μm) formed in the matrix and at grain boundaries (GB-B2).

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The experimental Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C-5Ni alloy was melted in an induction furnace.
Solution heat-treated for 35 min at 1250 °C in a protective argon atmosphere and then water quenched. This is the parent process of the annealing treatment.
The materials were cut into 3-mm (length), 3-mm (width) and 1-mm (thickness) samples.

Annealing treatments were conducted at 500 °C, 700 °C, 900 °C, and 1050 °C; the annealing holding time is not reported. This sample corresponds to the 500 °C treatment applied to the solution-treated Ni-containing alloy.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Nano-indentation carried out at a constant loading/unloading rate of 500 μN s-1 up to a maximum load of 10000 μN with a hold time of 20 s; each measurement in a particular phase repeated at least 25 times and in arrays of 50-70 indentations applied across the region of interest.

hardness.region: coarse NiAl-type B2 particles in γ

precipitates.distribution: bands replacing the prior α (ferrite) phase

microstructure_list.region: prior α (ferrite) bands, replaced by B2 stringer bands

structures.overall_structure: Duplex microstructure of the Ni-containing alloy after annealing at 500 °C: an austenite (γ) matrix containing nano-sized cuboidal κ-carbide in the γ grain interiors, coarse B2 particles (2–7 μm) in the matrix and along grain boundaries (GB-B2), and B2 stringer bands that replaced the prior α (ferrite) phase.

unmapped_findings: The same alloy appears as Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C-5Ni in the text (b0008, b0017) but as Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5C-5Ni in Tables 1 and 2 (b0022, b0032), which appears to be a typographic inconsistency in the carbon content (0.5 vs 0.8) rather than a different sample.

At lower annealing temperatures (including 500 °C) the materials showed low ductility (elongation ≈10%) and increasing the annealing temperature improved the strength-ductility balance, per the authors' previous study (ref 11) cited in b0014.
The nano-indentation technique used cannot measure the hardness of isolated nano-sized precipitates; it yields a compound hardness value of the matrix together with the particles (b0026, b0042).
For the Ni-containing coarse B2 particles in γ, the measured Ni content was 8.2 wt.% at 500 °C (and 10.1 wt.% at 1050 °C), indicating the B2 composition varies with annealing temperature (b0040).

The Orowan mechanism was invoked to explain higher hardness at higher annealing temperatures: the increase in shear stress Δτ is proportional to the inverse of precipitate diameter (Δτ ∝ R^-1.25), i.e. smaller precipitates increase shear resistance (b0039).
In the presence of Ni, the peak hardness increased from 7.2 GPa to 9 GPa relative to the Ni-free alloy (b0059), attributed to replacement of Fe-Al bonds by stronger Ni-Al bonds in the B2 phase.
